Rule Contents: Calls to SAP standard subroutines (FORM routines) must not be performed
All development, including descriptions and comments, must be written in English.
All variables declared in ABAP must be explicitly typed.
Input parameters must use appropriate data elements.
All selection-screen parameters and select-options must be typed.
Free text types (such as STRING, BLOB, or long string types) must not be used for anything other than comments.
The error-handling section must not be empty and must contain appropriate error-handling logic.
Any caught exception must be either propagated to the caller (program, function, class) or handled appropriately.
Custom error pages must not disclose applicative or infrastructure details, such as stack traces or technical dumps.
Errors must be translated into understandable and user-friendly messages for end users.
Exception return codes (SY-SUBRC) must be checked when calling function modules or BAPIs that define exceptions.
Errors raised by class methods must be handled using TRY/CATCH blocks.
The exception class CX_ROOT must not be used.
RFC standard exceptions such as SYSTEM_FAILURE and COMMUNICATION_FAILURE must be explicitly used and handled.
New function modules or class methods should use exceptions as required.
